column3: title card
column5: F: Purchasing and stock replenishment. | M: Buying goods, moving them between shops, and topping up when they run low. We will follow one ordinary working day in the ERP.

column3: chapter card 1: buying (order, receive, pay)
column5: F: First, buying. In every business it goes the same way. You order the goods, you receive them, and later you pay the bill. | M: Three documents: a purchase order, a receipt, and a vendor invoice. This ERP follows iDempiere, so every step looks and behaves just as it does there.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT console.offerRows=1 · plugin.installed state=ACTIVE (org.kernel.friendly-ops)
column5: M: Before we start, one optional extra. This ERP grows through plugins, and they are listed behind this link, Plugins and Releases. | F: We install a shortcut plugin, called Friendly operations, with one click. It is off until you choose it, and everything we do first works without it.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT poA Seed Farm, header
column5: F: Now we log in as the shop's administrator and open the Purchase Order window. A purchase order is simply our promise to a supplier. | M: We start a new one, pick the supplier, Seed Farm, and the company, and save the header.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT poA={"d":"800003","s":"CO"} Mulch, qty 5
column5: M: Then the line: what we are buying. Five bags of mulch. | F: Save the line, go back to the order, and press Complete. Completing is what turns a draft into a real, binding order, and the order shows as Completed.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT infowin.rows=1 · receipt.lines q=3 linked to the order line · count.legacy=13 · mulch.onhandAfterReceipt delta 3
column5: M: The goods arrive, and we record that on a Material Receipt. A receipt can pull its lines straight from the order. | F: This button, Create Lines From, opens a search window with everything still waiting to arrive. We choose the order and tick the line. Only three bags came, so we type a three. | M: Run it, and the receipt has its line, linked to the order. Complete it, and three bags are on the shelf. That took thirteen steps from opening the window. Remember the number.

column3: chapter card 2: the shortcut; second order typed behind it
column5: F: Receiving goods is such a common job that there is a shortcut for it. Behind this card we have typed a second order: same supplier, same product, already completed. | M: The shortcut is optional. Like everything we add, it lives in the gear menu, where iDempiere keeps a document's processes.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT run.FO_Order_Receive ok (receipt CO, 5 bags) · run.FO_Order_Bill ok (invoice CO 13.5) · gear after = Copy Lines only
column5: M: We open the gear. Because this order is completed and still waiting for its goods, the menu offers Receive. | F: One click, and the receipt is made, filled and completed for us. All five bags are on the shelf. | M: Now the gear offers Create Bill, which turns the receipt into the supplier's invoice. And once it is billed, the menu stops offering it.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT count.legacy=13 · count.FO_Order_Receive=3 (read from this take's click tally)
column5: F: Counted in this very film. Thirteen steps the standard way, three with the shortcut. | M: Underneath, it is the same receipt process, so nothing new has to be learned or trusted.

column3: chapter card 3: moving stock; in-transit move typed behind it; fixture disclosed
column5: F: Next, moving stock. Bigger businesses have several warehouses, and goods travel between them. | M: That is an Inventory Move. When the goods are on a truck, the move is marked in transit: they have left one place and not yet arrived at the other. | F: Behind this card we typed one move: ten elm trees from the head office warehouse to Store Central. That document type is one we added to our own copy for this demo.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT move.afterComplete IP + confirm DR · stock.inTransit source 15 target 0
column5: M: We press Complete, and notice it does not finish. The move stays In Progress, and the system has made a confirmation for the shop to fill in when the goods arrive. | F: Now look at the stock. Nothing has moved. Fifteen elm trees still sit at head office, and none at the store. That is what in transit means: the goods are on the books, but on neither shelf.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT confirm.line.saved target 10 confirmed 8 scrapped 1 difference 2 · after.confirm CO/CO
column5: F: Here is the shop's confirmation, in the Move Confirmation window. The line says ten were sent. | M: The shop counts. Eight arrived, and one of those was damaged, so it is scrapped. We type eight and one, and save. The system works out the difference by itself: two trees never arrived. | F: Then Complete. That finishes the confirmation and the move together.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT inventory.docs (store: scrapped 1; head office: difference 2), both CO
column5: M: Completing also wrote two small inventory documents. This one records the single scrapped tree, at Store Central. | F: And this one records the two trees that never arrived, back at head office. Nothing is simply deleted; every missing tree has a document.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT elm.before 15/0 · elm.after 5/7 · differenceDoc 2 · scrappedDoc 1 · elm.conserved=true · books.balanced
column5: F: So where did the ten go? Head office went from fifteen to five. The store has seven. Two are written off as lost, and one as scrapped. | M: Every tree is accounted for, and the accounting entries balance.

column3: chapter card 4: topping up (min and max levels)
column5: M: And now the question every shop asks: when do we buy more? | F: Every product has a lowest and a highest stock level. The Replenish Report compares them with what is on the shelf, and proposes how much to order.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT docTypeOptions (Purchase Order offered only after Create is chosen)
column5: F: We open the Replenish Report and choose the head office warehouse. | M: Then we say what to create: purchase orders. Only now does a Document Type box appear, because only now is it needed.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT levels (Elm Tree 5/10/20, Mulch 58/40/75) read from m_replenish + stock
column5: M: We press Run. While it works, here is what it is checking. Every product has a lowest level and a highest level. | F: Elm trees: only five on the shelf, below the lowest level of ten, so they need ordering. The highest level is twenty, so the report will ask for fifteen. | M: Mulch, which we received earlier, has plenty. It sits inside its range, so the report leaves it alone. | F: Each product also has a rule for how to top up: manually, reorder when below the minimum, or keep it filled to the maximum. | M: And we choose what to create: a purchase order to a supplier, a requisition, a movement from another warehouse, or a production order. Today, purchase orders. Whatever you pick, the report only drafts documents. | F: In a real shop there are thousands of products, and nobody walks every shelf. The report also counts what customers have already reserved, and what we have already ordered from suppliers, so we do not order twice for the same need. | M: Think of it as a very patient stock-taker. It looks at the shelf, at the promises made to customers, and at the orders on the way, and then writes a shopping list for the buyer. | F: The buyer stays in charge. Drafts can be changed, merged or thrown away before anything goes to a supplier. | M: Running all of that takes a little while, so let us give it a moment.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT replenish.result OK #3 · replenish.elm q=15 · replenish.orders 3 DR
column5: F: Done. The report made three purchase orders, and elm trees are on the list, fifteen of them, exactly as expected.

column3: §ERP_FILM_FACT lastPO draft; replenish.orders
column5: M: Here is one of the orders it created, a draft. Nobody has promised a supplier anything yet; a person still reviews it and presses Complete. | F: One thing to know. Drafts do not count as on order, so running the report again before completing them would propose the same goods again. iDempiere does exactly this, and so does our copy.

column3: §PURCH_FACT parity card (createfrom, matchpo, movement_facts, confirm, inventory, replenish) read from witness logs
column5: F: Everything in this film was checked against the real iDempiere, the ERP this one copies. | M: The card shows how many cases matched: receipt lines, purchase order matches, inventory postings, confirmations, physical count documents, and the Replenish Report, row for row. | F: And while filming, we found three gaps in our own screens. We fixed them, and they are tested now too.
